glacier-fieldwork.caption: A researcher records measurements on Olympic’s glacier ice. A field observation becomes part of a longer record.
glacier-fieldwork.alt: A researcher kneels on a snowy glacier and writes measurements on a datasheet.
glacier-fieldwork.rights: NPS-origin image, no third-party restriction indicated on the source page. https://www.nps.gov/aboutus/disclaimer.htm

visual-ozette-memory.caption: An object is not its whole story. Evidence gains meaning through context and the people who interpret it. Original explanatory illustration; schematic, not a measured dataset.
visual-ozette-memory.alt: A generic woven fragment, a record sheet and a group of people represent material evidence, recorded context and community interpretation. No specific Makah artifact is depicted.
visual-ozette-memory.rights: Original SVG illustration created for Nathan Wilson’s ORB Journeys.

visual-seafloor-to-summit.caption: Oceanic material becomes mountain terrain. Subduction, accretion and uplift are distinct parts of the explanation. Original explanatory illustration; schematic, not a measured dataset.
visual-seafloor-to-summit.alt: A conceptual cross-section shows an oceanic plate descending beneath North America, sediments accumulating at the margin and uplifted terrain above. Not to scale.
visual-seafloor-to-summit.rights: Original SVG illustration created for Nathan Wilson’s ORB Journeys.

visual-rain-shadow.caption: A mountain barrier divides the weather. Windward and leeward exposure help create different growing conditions. Original explanatory illustration; schematic, not a measured dataset.
visual-rain-shadow.alt: Moist Pacific air rises on a mountain’s windward side, with rain drawn beneath clouds; drier air descends on the opposite side. Regional pattern, not a weather forecast.
visual-rain-shadow.rights: Original SVG illustration created for Nathan Wilson’s ORB Journeys.

visual-salmon-life.caption: One life connects several habitats. Timing and freshwater needs vary among salmon species and populations. Original explanatory illustration; schematic, not a measured dataset.
visual-salmon-life.alt: A conceptual loop connects freshwater eggs, juvenile fish, an estuary, ocean growth and returning adults. It is a general life-cycle illustration, not a species-specific schedule.
visual-salmon-life.rights: Original SVG illustration created for Nathan Wilson’s ORB Journeys.

visual-ocean-in-the-forest.caption: The ocean’s nutrients travel upstream. Returning fish connect marine production with freshwater food webs. Original explanatory illustration; schematic, not a measured dataset.
visual-ocean-in-the-forest.alt: Returning salmon carry material from an ocean panel toward a stream and trees. A separate lower arrow shows water moving downstream. No proportional nutrient contribution is implied.
visual-ocean-in-the-forest.rights: Original SVG illustration created for Nathan Wilson’s ORB Journeys.

visual-sediment-to-sea.caption: Sediment continues beyond the river mouth. Reconnection can change the shoreline and the seabed. Original explanatory illustration; schematic, not a measured dataset.
visual-sediment-to-sea.alt: A river reaches the coast and branches across a fan of deposited sediment. This is a conceptual delta illustration, not an aerial image or measured map of the Elwha.
visual-sediment-to-sea.rights: Original SVG illustration created for Nathan Wilson’s ORB Journeys.

visual-floor-ice.caption: A stream has more than one water source. The research question concerns the size and timing of changing contributions. Original explanatory illustration; schematic, not a measured dataset.
visual-floor-ice.alt: Three distinct water sources—ice and snow, rain and subsurface water—connect to a stream. Arrows are conceptual and do not show measured quantities.
visual-floor-ice.rights: Original SVG illustration created for Nathan Wilson’s ORB Journeys.

visual-floor-forest.caption: Which process explains a changing forest?. Repeated plots can connect vegetation changes with local conditions. Original explanatory illustration; schematic, not a measured dataset.
visual-floor-forest.alt: Different tree plots appear on opposite mountain slopes, next to a checklist of snow duration, plant timing, seedling survival and disturbance. No observed trend is plotted.
visual-floor-forest.rights: Original SVG illustration created for Nathan Wilson’s ORB Journeys.

visual-floor-marmot.caption: Not seen is not always absent. A hypothetical survey pattern shows why repeat visits matter. Original explanatory illustration; schematic, not a measured dataset.
visual-floor-marmot.alt: An explicitly hypothetical three-by-three matrix shows detections and nondetections across meadow patches and repeat visits. It contains no real marmot survey data.
visual-floor-marmot.rights: Original SVG illustration created for Nathan Wilson’s ORB Journeys.

visual-floor-salmon.caption: From a reopened route to a lasting population. Each recovery claim needs evidence matched to its scale. Original explanatory illustration; schematic, not a measured dataset.
visual-floor-salmon.alt: Three ascending stages distinguish fish passage, reproduction and persistence across generations. This is an evidence framework, not a plotted recovery trajectory.
visual-floor-salmon.rights: Original SVG illustration created for Nathan Wilson’s ORB Journeys.

visual-floor-coast.caption: Several pressures can leave similar signals. The challenge is to distinguish patterns from their causes. Original explanatory illustration; schematic, not a measured dataset.
visual-floor-coast.alt: A schematic tidepool and sensor are surrounded by temperature, water chemistry, exposure and natural-variability labels. No stressor is assigned a measured effect.
visual-floor-coast.rights: Original SVG illustration created for Nathan Wilson’s ORB Journeys.

visual-floor-quinault.caption: Make the data gap specific. A useful investigation connects a measurement with a real decision. Original explanatory illustration; schematic, not a measured dataset.
visual-floor-quinault.alt: A schematic lake cross-section with a fish and sampling line connects to three questions about missing information, decisions and who guides priorities. It is not a bathymetric map of Lake Quinault.
visual-floor-quinault.rights: Original SVG illustration created for Nathan Wilson’s ORB Journeys.
